photoDiagram.a11yCaption: Sunlight reaches a flowering plant, which gives food to a pollinator and gets pollen carried. Separately, fungi break down leaf litter and return nutrients to the soil. Then the one word hornbill branches into four named species, each with a photograph: Rufous-necked, Oriental Pied, Great and Wreathed. Last, the two things hornbills depend on: large, old trees and specific fruits.

flags: Uses the new photoDiagram companion field (docs/photo-diagrams.md, PhotoDiagram.js) - the engine facility built specifically to replace this slide's original hand-rolled DomSimulation (BiodiversityLinksScene.js, zero real CONTROLS/interactivity). Real, licensed Wikimedia Commons photos throughout (credited in media/L01/photo-credits.txt), live per-photo alt text, live theme support, no baked pixels.

Uses photoDiagram's revealAt (progressive reveal, added specifically for this slide after an initial single-diagram draft rendered every photo too small to read): ecology nodes have the default revealAt 0 (visible from mediaStep's own gate), the hornbill root + 4 species nodes carry revealAt: 1, so they only appear once the 'Open the Bird Record' beat is reached - and the diagram's auto-fit viewBox recomputes from only the currently-revealed nodes at each beat, so beat 0's three ecology photos render large in a tight crop instead of sharing a canvas sized for the eventual full (7-photo) diagram. Restores the same beat-paced reveal the block had with reveal.images, without that mechanism's non-sticky-per-step-id gotcha (see GENERATION-LOG.md).

Beat 2 ('Record the Relationship') gets its own distinct visual, not a frozen repeat of beat 1's photos: three icon-labelled evidence nodes (nesting/fruit/diet-unsure) at revealAt: 2, no photos of their own (this content is conceptual, not figurative - per docs/simulation-authoring.md's own image-vs-nothing guidance for a pure informational callout, a photo here would be decorative, not informative). 'unsure' deliberately carries no tone (renders as a plain muted chip, not a toned one) - the visual distinction stands in for the old DomSimulation's dashed-border 'still uncertain' styling; photoDiagram has no dashed-node variant yet, flagged here rather than adding one speculatively for a single use.
